result.title: Discovering Learning Rules that Shape Others
result.summary: In general-sum games, self-interested learners can reach outcomes that are poor for everyone, which has motivated methods that shape the opponent's learning. Methods like Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness (LOLA), which differentiates through the opponent's learning process, and Model-Free Opponent Shaping (M-FOS), which uses model-free optimisation methods for long-horizon opponent shaping, have enabled mutual cooperation and exploitation of learners. However, these methods require access to the opponent's parameters, policy, rewards or learning rule during deployment. In single-agent reinforcement learning, update rules discovered by meta-learning have achieved state-of-the-art results (e.g. DiscoRL). These rules are separate from the policy they train and read only the agent's own experience. We hereby extend this framework to general-sum settings by introducing Discovered Update Rule for Opponent Shaping (DUOS). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first method to discover an update rule for an agent in general-sum games. DUOS meta-trains the rule to maximise the agent's expected return over its lifetime, and updates an inner network using the agent's own experience. We show that our discovered rule exhibits behaviour consistent with opponent shaping without reading opponent policies or parameters, and ranks 1st in normalised mean score and 1st in self-play among tournament entrants.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DUOS，把「元学习发现更新规则」的框架从单智能体扩展到一般和博弈：仅凭自身经验元训练一条与策略分离的更新规则，目标是最大化智能体终身期望回报，并在锦标赛的归一化均分与自博弈中排名第一。
AI.relevance_reason: 「元学习出一条只读自身经验、独立于策略的更新规则」这一概念形式，可能与 LVR 中如何学习 latent 推理状态的更新规则、以及长程轨迹上的贡献分配与监督相关，可供核查其规则结构与训练目标；但多智能体对手塑造设定距视觉推理较远，迁移属推测。
